summary.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready.” It is the standardized simplified form of 備, whose older graph is interpreted as a person with an arrow container, an image associated with preparedness.

formation.text: The received analysis treats 備 as phonosemantic: 人 depicts a person, while 𤰈 is interpreted as an arrow container and assigned a sound role. The person carrying the container is associated with readiness. The sound analysis is traditional, though the historical pronunciation of 𤰈 has not been independently established. Another interpretation treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.

components.text: In one analysis of 備, 人 depicts the person carrying the arrow container. Another account interprets the whole graph as a quiver picture.
In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as arrows in a container. The received analysis also assigns it a sound role, though the historical sound relation is not independently verified.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin match does not establish the historical sound relation; no independent historical pronunciation for 𤰈 was verified.

sound.text: Both 𤰈 and 備 are read bèi in modern Mandarin. This present-day match is compatible with the received sound analysis but does not verify its historical basis.

history.text: 備 is recorded in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories. These categories do not establish the graph’s earliest appearance or a dated sequence among the forms.

In bronze forms, the lower part of 𤰈 is reported to change to 用; this has been tentatively interpreted as a sound element. The modern printed form 𤰇 is described as a change from seal-script 𤰈, without a dated sequence established between these forms.
The 1956 simplification scheme standardized 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 is documented as a variant of 備, but the proposed derivation of 备 specifically from 俻 is not established.

uncertainties.text: The person-carrying-a-quiver interpretation links 備 with readiness but does not establish the word’s earliest meaning. 備 is also reported as a whole-graph sound-based borrowing for 箙, “quiver,” in a bronze inscription; the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are unrecovered, so that proposed sound match cannot be verified.

Reported uses include “prepared” or “complete,” “for use,” “cautious,” “equipment,” and “all” or “entirely.” The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or a continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver interpretation may explain the association with preparedness, but does not prove this was the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss includes “cautious” or “careful”; it does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.
A bronze inscription reportedly reuses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver.” The proposed sound-based borrowing does not verify that 箙 sounded like the pictured container’s unrecovered original name.
